gap_description: Barter, unregistered work, informal credit, undeclared trade and other activity are weakly observed.
why_it_matters: Formal economic statistics can miss substantial local activity.
attack_strategy: Compare household surveys, tax gaps, labour-force surveys, transaction studies and source-specific estimates.
falsification_question: Would the apparent economic structure remain if plausible informal activity were included?
alternative_explanations: Measurement under-reporting; definitional differences; illegal activity hidden by design.

gap_description: Actual local venues, independent media, festivals, clubs and amateur groups are not equivalent to consumption measures.
why_it_matters: Consumption can remain high while local production capacity erodes.
attack_strategy: Build place-time inventories of active organisations, facilities, participants, outputs and survival.
falsification_question: Does high consumption persist after local production capacity falls?
alternative_explanations: Migration; digitisation; consolidation; changes in reporting.

gap_description: Places may be discussed extensively while producing little local journalism or agenda-setting information.
why_it_matters: External attention is not the same as local voice.
attack_strategy: Separate about/by/for/with-place information and compare local versus external contribution and attention.
falsification_question: Does high external attention predict local information capacity, or can the two diverge?
alternative_explanations: Tourism; crisis coverage; platform effects; population size.

gap_description: Formal education counts do not capture practical skills, maintenance capacity, organisation or institutional memory.
why_it_matters: Capability stocks can erode before outputs visibly decline.
attack_strategy: Measure practitioners, transmission, retirement/exit, maintenance and institutional-memory indicators.
falsification_question: Can observed capability decline be distinguished from changing demand or technology substitution?
alternative_explanations: Automation; migration; ageing; changing task requirements.

gap_description: Local extraction, imports, processing, waste, recycling and exports are poorly represented compared with national aggregates.
why_it_matters: A place's physical metabolism can differ sharply from national averages.
attack_strategy: Track directed material flows with quantity, processing stage, destination and recovery status.
falsification_question: Does the apparent prosperity of a place persist when physical inputs, waste and exports are included?
alternative_explanations: Boundary choice; supply-chain relocation; accounting conventions.

gap_description: Security provision can be distributed among state, private, community, militia, religious, customary and criminal providers.
why_it_matters: Recorded crime alone cannot describe who actually provides security or coercive capacity.
attack_strategy: Map provider presence, functions, coverage, reliance and relationships to other providers.
falsification_question: Do changes in recorded crime remain after changes in security-provider structure are accounted for?
alternative_explanations: Reporting changes; enforcement intensity; conflict; institutional substitution.

gap_description: Annual indicators can miss rapid transitions and regime shifts.
why_it_matters: Boom, decline, reconstruction and consolidation can occur between annual observations.
attack_strategy: Use event/change-point metadata and non-annual observations where defensible.
falsification_question: Would the inferred transition timing change materially with monthly/quarterly data?
alternative_explanations: Seasonality; reporting delays; boundary changes; temporary shocks.

gap_description: Variable definitions, boundaries and denominators change over time and across sources.
why_it_matters: Apparent trends may be measurement artefacts.
attack_strategy: Require definition, methodology, denominator, boundary and source-vintage metadata.
falsification_question: Does the relationship survive a defensible harmonisation or source-stratified analysis?
alternative_explanations: Real change; reclassification; survey redesign; boundary revisions.

gap_description: Proposed patterns can become stories if alternative explanations and falsification tests are not required.
why_it_matters: Epistemic guardrails are necessary for autonomous discovery.
attack_strategy: Require alternative explanations, confounders, reverse causality, selection bias, measurement change and falsification tests.
falsification_question: What observation would make the obvious interpretation wrong?
alternative_explanations: Confirmation bias; collider bias; omitted variables; model selection.

gap_description: Cross-border cultural influence needs exposure, consumption, adoption, local reproduction, hybridisation and return-flow measures.
why_it_matters: A single cultural-share number hides direction and mutation.
attack_strategy: Track directed place-time flows and variant parentage.
falsification_question: Does an apparent foreign-origin influence disappear when local reproduction and hybridisation are separated?
alternative_explanations: Common global platforms; language; migration; ownership; production location.
